answer: Each identity claims a lagoon dock cleat and locks a 70-credit bond, sealed by a saffron stamp on cleat and key. Each epoch it is pull-tested and the force noted. A horizon auditor recomputes expected force from the public cleat table by line angle and age, in 3%; a miss or reuse burns the bond. First fee 36; the k-th fake pays 36+6(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 6,030; 1,000 clones lock 70,000 and pay 3,033,000. A rented-cleat ring fails: a rented cleat carries its owner's saffron stamp, so a second key on it is refused and both burn. An honest agent pays 36 once, reclaiming the bond when clean.
